# Introduction

This file is used to conduct multinomial regression analysis on the survey responses of Recreational fishers from the SELTMP in 2025

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
	echo = TRUE,
	include = TRUE,
	message = FALSE,
	warning = FALSE)

rm(list=ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library("gert")
library("usethis")
library("here")
library("tidyverse")
library("readxl")
library("emmeans")
library("nnet")
```

```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet
raw_data <- read_excel(here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Sept-22-2026.xlsx"), sheet = "Raw_Data")

##glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
emm_options(df = Inf) #Force every summary/test/CI below to use df = Inf (normal distribution)

# Filter data for fisher status
fisher_data <- raw_data |>
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == "Y")  |>
    mutate(inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = FALSE))  #Set to false for multinomial regression

# Set up variable to run regression against
fisher_data <- fisher_data |>
  mutate(
  educ = factor(educ, levels = 1:7, ordered = FALSE)            # use for categorical question
  # q_b = as.numeric(q_a)       # use for numeric question
  ) |>
  drop_na(educ)
```
  
## Run multinomial logistic regression model  
```{r}
multi_model <- multinom(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = fisher_data)
summary(multi_model)

# Since multinom() doesn't report p-values, will need to compute them manually
z_vals <- summary(multi_model)$coefficients / summary(multi_model)$standard.errors
p_vals <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_vals)))
p_vals
```

## Predict probability of each rating, by fisher status
```{r}
emm_prob_nom <- emmeans(multi_model, ~ educ | inter_zoning, mode = "prob")
summary(emm_prob_nom)
```

## Plot probability of each rating with confidence intervals
```{r}
emmip(multi_model, educ ~ inter_zoning, mode = "prob", dodge = 1.5, CIs = TRUE) +
       labs(title = str_wrap("Predicted Probability of Each MPA Support Rating by Education Level)" , width = 30), 
       x = "Rating (1-10)", y = "Predicted Probability") 
```
